title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Budget cut motion for Head I
sections.summary: A motion proposes reducing the total sum allocated for Head I of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: Fresh Start programme for families
sections.summary: The Fresh Start programme lets families buy a 2-room flexi flat on a shorter lease with housing loans up to $35,000 and HDB Concessionary Loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: If we are doing well and strong, we lend a hand to those who need it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And one of the most inspiring and practical ways in which we strive to do this is the relatively new Fresh Start programme which allows families to buy a 2-room flexi flat on a shorter lease and they can get their housing loans of up to $35,000 and the Housing and Development Board (HDB) Concessionary Loans.

sections.label: Scheme features and employment strings
sections.summary: The scheme ties to stable employment for financial sustainability and job incentives, and has 11 key features including a 20-year minimum occupation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Strings on stable employment to ensure financial sustainability as well as to incentivise people to look for jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But the scheme itself has 11 key features, including the fact that there is a minimum occupation period of 20 years.

sections.label: Joint MSF and MND scheme
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MSF and MND set up a joint scheme with an officer combining social welfare, housing, financial and rules expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I make the point about the complexity of HDB rules not to ask for them to be made fewer, but for their application to be simpler.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Ministry of National Development (MND) set up a joint scheme and produce a magic mix – someone who is part social welfare officer, part housing agent, part financial consultant and, above all, an expert in navigating through the rules.

sections.label: Support for homeless who declined
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry is doing to strengthen support for homeless people who declined assistance, and notes a middle-class complaint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What is the Ministry doing to strengthen support for homeless people who declined assistance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: At a recent post-Budget dinner, a gentleman approached me to lament how he thought the middle-class, like him, was unfairly treated.

sections.label: Fairness and social equity questions
sections.summary: Anecdotes about neighbours receiving assistance despite being cash-rich or supported by extended family called into question fairness and social equity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is not uncommon to hear similar lamentations, even HDB residents sometimes asked us why certain neighbours received financial assistance or more Government benefits when the said neighbours are cash-rich or already were supported by extended family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: These anecdotes called into the question the concept of fairness and social equity.

sections.label: More precise personalised public assistance
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will consider a more precise and personalised public assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Is a more precise and personalised public assistance an idea that the Ministry will consider?

sections.label: MSF study of MSO model
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSF will study the MSO model and adopt relevant principles and features for a similar SSO model led by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will MSF study the MSO model and adopt the relevant principles and features for a similar SSO model led by the Minister himself?

sections.label: Extending cash gift to single mothers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSF can consider extending the cash gift to single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MSF consider also extending the cash gift to our single mothers?

sections.label: KidSTART pilot, families and CYPA age
sections.summary: The passage states the three-year pilot's expected beneficiaries, Budget Speech figures on KidSTART families, and welcomes a proposed CYPA amendment raising the protection cut-off age from 16 to 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The three-year pilot was expected to benefit about 1,000 children living in the pilot regions of Kreta Ayer, Bukit Merah, Taman Jurong, Boon Lay and Geylang Serai.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last month, the Minister for Finance mentioned in his Budget Speech that more than 900 families had received support from KidSTART since 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the topic of youths, I welcome the Ministry's announcement last month that it is proposing amending the Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) to increase the cut-off age for protection from 16 to 18 years.

sections.label: Youth re-offending and national committee
sections.summary: The passage states re-offending within three years fell from 20.3% to 16.7%, still high, and that the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism was set up in April last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While latest figures have shown a drop in the percentage of youths that re-offend within three years of their incarceration, from 20.3% to the current 16.7%, this is still a high figure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To help at-risk youths break away from the vicious cycle of crime, the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism was set up in April last year to look into how we can intervene upstream and adopt a more preventive and integrative approach towards at-risk youths, young offenders, as well as their families.

sections.label: Survey of people living on streets
sections.summary: The passage states a survey by SW101 and Montford Care found 180 people living on the streets one night, with two-thirds employed, over a quarter owning a flat and a quarter married.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a survey done by volunteer group SW101 and a voluntary welfare organisation (VWO) Montford Care a little over a year ago, of the 180 people found living on the streets one night in Singapore, two-thirds have a job, more than a quarter own a flat and a quarter were married.

sections.label: Children adopted in Singapore halved
sections.summary: The number of children adopted in Singapore has halved this decade compared to the previous decade, with 352 adoptions in 2014 versus 731 in 2004.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, compared to the decade before, the number of children adopted in Singapore has halved in this decade.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, 352 children were adopted in 2014, compared to 731 children in 2004.

sections.label: Informing pregnant mothers about adoption
sections.summary: The speaker asks MSF to inform pregnant mothers considering terminations about adoption, calling it a win-win-win for baby, mother and adoptive parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would MSF please take up my suggestion of actively informing pregnant mothers, who are considering terminations, of the loving and nurturing option of giving their baby up for adoption?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is a win-win-win formula because, one, it would give the baby a shot at life in a loving and nurturing family environment; two, the pregnant mother benefits from a wider and longer list of options for her to consider; and, three, the adoptive parents benefit from fulfilling their wish to raise a child in a loving environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Important changes had been introduced as a result of these Masterplans.

sections.label: Five-step approach to support caregivers
sections.summary: At the recent debate on the Parliamentary Motion on strengthening support for caregivers, the speaker had proposed a five-step approach to support caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: At the recent debate on the Parliamentary Motion on strengthening support for caregivers, I had proposed a five-step approach to support caregivers on the ground.

sections.label: Enhanced early intervention for children
sections.summary: Earlier this year, MSF announced enhanced early intervention for children with developmental needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, MSF announced enhanced early intervention for children with developmental needs.

sections.label: Customised early intervention implementation questions
sections.summary: The speaker asks how customised early intervention will be implemented, how MSF will keep its quality on par with international standards, and how continuity of support is ensured for special needs students transitioning to mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, important that we put in effort to curate the best support and curriculum for our children with needs, to ensure the best possible outcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to find out more details about how the customised early intervention would be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, how can MSF ensure that the quality of the early intervention is kept on par with international standards?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in my maiden Adjournment Motion as a backbencher, I spoke about how important it is that we always "see through the eyes of our people".

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, how do we, as a society, ensure continuity of support for our special needs students who transition into mainstream schools?

sections.label: Private transport cost for wheelchair
sections.summary: Her mum found that private transport for N and her wheelchair would cost $750 to $1,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Her mum looked around and found out that private transport for N and her wheelchair would cost $750 to $1,000 a month.

sections.label: Ageing population and special needs
sections.summary: As the population grows older, more seniors will have grown-up special needs children still needing extra care and support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as our population grows older, there will be more seniors in our community who have grown-up special needs children still needing that extra care and support.

sections.label: Population and senior projections
sections.summary: Projections put the population at 6.34 million by 2030, with 28% being citizens above 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to projections, our population is expected to reach 6.34 million by the year 2030, out of which, 28% would be senior citizens above the age of 65.

sections.label: LPA certificate issuer categories
sections.summary: LPAs are executed before an LPA certificate issuer from three professional categories: accredited medical professionals, registered psychiatrists, and practising lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: LPAs are to be executed before an LPA certificate issuer who can come from three categories of professionals: one, medical professionals who are accredited by the Public Guardian; two, registered psychiatrists; and three, practising lawyers.

sections.label: Early childhood subsidies application process
sections.summary: The Government provides generous subsidies for early childhood services, but the application process can be difficult to navigate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Government provides generous subsidies for early childhood services, but the application process can be difficult to navigate.

sections.label: Childcare subsidy access hurdles
sections.summary: Parents could pay as low as $5 a month in childcare fees but face multiple hurdles to maximum subsidies, including work requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Though their parents could pay as low as $5 a month in childcare fees, they face multiple hurdles in accessing the maximum level of subsidies, including having to meet certain requirements for work.

sections.label: Childcare access and parent employment
sections.summary: Whether children from low-income families can access such childcare services should not depend on their parents' employment status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whether these children from low-income families can access such childcare services should not be dependent on the employment status of their parents.

sections.label: Subsidies for working mothers
sections.summary: The passage asks why families with non-working mothers receive less subsidies than families with working mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Why do we provide less subsidies to families with non-working mothers and more subsidies to families with working mothers?

sections.label: Preschool closures and mergers
sections.summary: The passage asks how many preschools have closed, been acquired or merged since the Act was passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, how many preschools have closed down or been acquired or merged since the Act was passed?

sections.label: Singapore early education benchmarks
sections.summary: The passage asks how Singapore has recently fared in international early education benchmarks since the Starting Well study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, it has been over six years since the Starting Well study by the Economist Intelligence Unit commissioned by the Lien Foundation ranked Singapore 29th out of 45 countries studied in terms of early education sector quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How has Singapore fared in such international benchmarks recently?

sections.label: Operators using IT grants
sections.summary: The passage asks whether many operators tapped Government grants to defray part of the costs of adopting IT solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Have there been many operators who tapped on the available Government grants to defray part of the costs for adopting IT solutions?

sections.label: Projected early childhood educators
sections.summary: The passage states that by 2020 the number of early childhood educators is projected to reach 20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: By 2020, the number of early childhood educators is projected to reach 20,000.

sections.label: Council for Board Diversity
sections.summary: The passage asks how the newly formed Council for Board Diversity will build on the Diversity Action Committee's progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For example, the Diversity Action Committee has made good progress in increasing women representation on corporate boards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: How will the newly formed Council for Board Diversity build on these efforts?

sections.label: Women on corporate boards
sections.summary: Asks for updates on the Diversity Action Committee, BoardAgender and the corporate governance code on board diversity disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Having more women on board can help companies entrench a stronger and more well-rounded human resource policy and can help attract potential women leaders boost their development and performance.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Diversity in corporate leadership has also been shown to promote better governance and sustained business performance.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the work of the Diversity Action Committee and the BoardAgender, and also an update on the code of corporate governance for Singapore Exchange-listed companies to disclose their board diversity policies?

sections.label: MSF priority areas
sections.summary: MSF will focus on three priority areas: social compact, inclusive society, and affordable quality preschool for children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) will focus on three priority areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, building a strong social compact, by strengthening family and community bonds and our collective resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, building a more inclusive society, to enable people of all abilities to achieve their fullest potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, giving our children a good start in life through affordable, accessible and quality preschool.

sections.label: ComLink and LCN support
sections.summary: Describes the Community Link for rental housing families and the Local Community Network pilot for at-risk youths and families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At the Joint Segment on Opportunity yesterday, I described the Community Link (ComLink) that we will be setting up to support rental housing families and the Local Community Network (LCN) pilot to wrap around support for at-risk youths and their families.

sections.label: Training frontline officers
sections.summary: By end of this year, 2,500 officers from frontline agencies will be trained to identify clients' broader needs and link them to agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: By the end of this year, we will train 2,500 officers from various frontline agencies to identify a client's broader needs and link the client to the relevant agencies.

sections.label: Services at 24 SSOs
sections.summary: By end of this year, clients can access financial, employment and housing services at all 24 SSOs, and legal advisory at three SSOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: By the end this year, clients will be able to access financial, employment and housing services at all our 24 SSOs, either through physical co-location of services or videoconferencing links with HDB, WSG and NTUC's e2i career coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: By the second quarter of this year, clients will be able to access legal advisory services through videoconferencing at Boon Lay, Taman Jurong and Queenstown SSOs.

sections.label: Automatic ComCare assessments
sections.summary: ComCare clients will be automatically considered for reduced HDB rental rates and assessed for MOE financial assistance and childcare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To enable ComCare clients to be automatically considered for reduced HDB rental rates and assessed concurrently for MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme for their school-going children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: By the second half of this year, ComCare clients with young children will also be automatically assessed for childcare subsidy and financial assistance.

sections.label: Training in new guidelines
sections.summary: About 200 agencies and 400 officers across seven towns are being trained in guidelines rolled out this month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: About 200 agencies and 400 officers across seven towns are being trained in these guidelines, which we have started rolling out this month.

sections.label: First networking round completion
sections.summary: The first round of networking, about 160 agencies and 200 officers per town, will be completed by July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The first round of networking, involving about 160 agencies and 200 officers per town, will be completed by July this year.

sections.label: Project Home Alone befriending programme
sections.summary: Project Home Alone began from a Hougang-Serangoon SG Cares session, with SSO Hougang, Ang Mo Kio-Hougang Grassroots and Xinmin Secondary School starting an elderly befriending programme last month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Project Home Alone (PHA), for example, is an initiative that sprung up from the Hougang-Serangoon SG Cares Community Network session in September last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The SSO at Hougang, the Ang Mo Kio-Hougang Grassroots and Xinmin Secondary School initiated an elderly befriending programme after they met during the session and it started last month.

sections.label: Lengthened post-care support
sections.summary: Jervin received his professional barista certificate before NS, and post-care support after discharge from MSF's Youth Homes is lengthened from two months to one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Jervin was also placed on the Bettr Barista Holistic Training Programme and received his professional barista certificate before he started NS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To better support young people like him, after their discharge from MSF's Youth Homes, we have decided to lengthen post-care support from two months to one year.

sections.label: Public consultations and amendment Bill
sections.summary: Public consultations run till mid-March, and the amendment Bill is to be tabled in Parliament later this year or early next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Our public consultations will run till mid-March, and we aim to table the amendment Bill in Parliament later this year or early next year.

sections.label: Transitional Shelters and Welfare Homes
sections.summary: Transitional Shelters offer temporary accommodation and social support to homeless persons, while Welfare Homes provide long-term residential care for destitute persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Transitional Shelters offer temporary accommodation and social support to homeless persons who need intensive support to access stable housing, while Welfare Homes provide long-term residential care for destitute persons who are unable to support themselves and lack family support.

sections.label: Funds for social support network
sections.summary: It places them in a better position to operate in a network environment of social support, the largest tranche of funds since 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It will also place them in a better position to operate in a network environment of social support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is the largest tranche of funds put in since it was set up in 2006.

sections.label: Social Service SkillsFuture Tripartite Taskforce
sections.summary: A Social Service SkillsFuture Tripartite Taskforce will be set up to coordinate and drive skills development initiatives in the social service sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Building on the framework, we will set up a Social Service SkillsFuture Tripartite Taskforce to coordinate and drive skills development initiatives in the social service sector.

sections.label: Benefits extended to unwed mothers
sections.summary: Following a 2016 review, 16 weeks of maternity leave and Child Development Account benefits, including the $3,000 First Step grant, were extended to unwed mothers and their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Arising from our review in 2016, we extended 16 weeks of maternity leave and the Child Development Account benefits, including the $3,000 First Step grant, to unwed mothers and their children.

sections.label: Pre-abortion counselling and consent
sections.summary: Women considering abortion must complete pre-abortion counselling and can give written consent only at least 48 hours after the session.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All women considering abortion are required to complete pre-abortion counselling, where a trained counsellor will share on the medical, psychosocial and emotional aspects of terminating pregnancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: She can only give her written consent to terminate pregnancy at least 48 hours after this session.

sections.label: Employment of residents aged 65
sections.summary: According to the 2018 Comprehensive Labour Force Survey, 27% of residents aged 65 and above were employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: According to the 2018 Comprehensive Labour Force Survey, 27% of residents aged 65 and above were employed.

sections.label: Special educational needs under Compulsory Education
sections.summary: From January this year, children with moderate to severe special educational needs were included under the Compulsory Education Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: From January this year, we have included children with moderate to severe special educational needs under the Compulsory Education Framework.

sections.label: Grandparent Caregiver Relief age limit
sections.summary: From Year of Assessment 2020, the age limit is removed for Grandparent Caregiver Relief for children with special needs, giving working mothers $3,000 relief regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: As announced by the Ministry of Finance, the age limit on children with special needs will also be removed for the Grandparent Caregiver Relief scheme, from the Year of Assessment 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Working mothers who seek the help of grandparents to take care of their children with special needs can get tax relief of $3,000, regardless of the child's age.

sections.label: Cross-sectoral workgroups for employability
sections.summary: Two cross-sectoral workgroups involving people, private and public sectors will focus on employability and independent living, the first on lifelong learning and employment pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Together, we can co-create the hardware, software and heartware of an inclusive Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, very happy to announce that we will form two cross-sectoral workgroups involving the people, private and public sector partners to focus on employability and independent living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The first workgroup will look at preparing persons with special needs for the future economy, by enhancing access to lifelong learning opportunities and employment pathways.

sections.label: Special Needs Trust Company support
sections.summary: The Special Needs Trust Company was set up to support parents and caregivers of persons with special needs in future care planning and financial security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about support for seniors who worry about their children with special needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We have set up the Special Needs Trust Company to support parents and caregivers of persons with special needs in future care planning and financial security.

sections.label: Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme
sections.summary: The PDD Scheme, launched in September last year, lets individuals engage registered PDDs for major decisions; 20 have registered, and MSF launched a two-year CKS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The first is the Professional Deputies and Donees (PDD) Scheme, which was launched in September last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, individuals can procure the services of a registered PDD to make major decisions on their behalf, such as liquidating their property to finance their care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Twenty individuals have registered as PDDs so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: MSF will continue to train more suitable persons to be PDDs and raise awareness of PDD services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: To complement the PDD scheme, MSF launched a two-year Community Kin Service (CKS).

sections.label: Third Enabling Masterplan life-stage approach
sections.summary: Under the third Enabling Masterplan, a life-stage approach will provide further support for those with special needs at various life stages to live independently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Under the third Enabling Masterplan, we will adopt a life-stage approach to provide further support for those with special needs at various stages of their lives, so that they are better able to live independently.

sections.label: Cross-sectoral workgroups for implementation
sections.summary: All of society across public, private and people sectors must work as one, so two cross-sectoral workgroups will be introduced to ensure plans are implemented successfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: To ensure that these plans are implemented successfully, all of society across the public, private and people sectors must work as one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Therefore, we will be introducing two cross-sectoral workgroups.

sections.label: CKS pilot launch
sections.summary: MSF launched a two-year CKS pilot in 2018 to complement the PDD scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: To complement the PDD scheme, MSF launched a two-year CKS pilot in 2018.

sections.label: First pilot case
sections.summary: The pilot's first case is a 78-year-old man living alone in a one-room flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The first case under the pilot programme is a 78-year-old man who lives alone in a one-room flat.

sections.label: Preschool subsidies review
sections.summary: MSF is reviewing preschool subsidies and will provide more subsidies for job-seeking mothers and mothers caring for young children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Low-income families receive the most subsidies and thus need to pay only a few dollars a month in school fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We are reviewing preschool subsidies to make it more affordable for parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: While this review is ongoing, I am pleased to announce that MSF will provide more subsidies for mothers who are looking for a job and who need to place their children in childcare centres first, or mothers who are unable to work because they are caring for a young child.

sections.label: Families benefiting from enhancements
sections.summary: Over 5,000 families will benefit from these enhancements from 1 March 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Through these enhancements, over 5,000 families will benefit from 1 March 2019.

sections.label: Lower early intervention fees
sections.summary: From 1 April 2019, most families will pay lower early intervention fees, reduced by 30% to 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From 1 April 2019, most families will be paying lower fees, a reduction of 30% to 70% for early intervention services.

sections.label: EIPIC children in preschools
sections.summary: EIPIC children with sufficient progress can receive early intervention at preschools, benefiting at least 4,500 children yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For example, children from EIPIC who have achieved sufficient progress, can receive early intervention at their preschools without having to go to an early intervention centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This enhancement is expected to benefit at least 4,500 children every year.

sections.label: Kindergarten fee assistance and childcare subsidies
sections.summary: KiFAS keeps out-of-pocket costs for low- and middle-income parents in Anchor Operator or MOE Kindergartens at a few dollars a month, and ECDA will give parents greater certainty on childcare subsidy amounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: And with the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS), the out-of-pocket cost for low- and middle-income parents who enrol their children in Anchor Operator or MOE Kindergartens is a few dollars a month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am also glad to announce that ECDA will give parents greater certainty on the amount of childcare subsidies they will receive.

sections.label: Households benefiting from enhancements
sections.summary: More than 5,000 households will benefit every year from these enhancements, starting from 1 March 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Through these enhancements, more than 5,000 households like Mdm Lee's will benefit every year, starting from 1 March 2019 this year.

sections.label: Mature workers occupational health assessment
sections.summary: ECDA will collaborate with the Health Promotion Board to commission an occupational health and safety assessment, aiming to do more for mature workers and enhance their career longevity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In particular, we hope to do more for our mature workers and enhance their career longevity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that ECDA will be collaborating with the Health Promotion Board to commission an occupational health and safety assessment.

sections.label: One form for subsidy applications
sections.summary: Parents will fill in just one form to apply for subsidies and financial assistance, smoothening the process for about 20,000 new families annually and halving time spent on applications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Parents will be required to fill in just one form to apply for subsidies and financial assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This will smoothen the application process for about 20,000 new families annually, and halve the time spent on subsidy applications.

sections.label: Early intervention fee reductions
sections.summary: From 1 April, early intervention fees will be reduced for most families, with reductions averaging between 30% and 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From 1 April, early intervention fees will be reduced for most families, with reductions averaging between 30% and 70%.

sections.label: Women on boards of SGX companies
sections.summary: Women's representation on boards of the Top 100 primary-listed SGX companies rose from 7.5% at end 2013 to 15.2% at end December 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The representation of women on boards of the Top 100 primary-listed companies on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) had increased from 7.5% at end 2013, before the DAC was constituted, to 15.2% at the end December 2018.

sections.label: Women on Statutory Boards
sections.summary: Women make up 23% of participation on Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Currently, we have 23% women participation on Statutory Boards.

sections.label: Singapore gender pay gap
sections.summary: MOM estimates Singapore's gender pay gap for full-time employed residents in similar occupation groups at around 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MOM’s latest data estimates Singapore’s gender pay gap for full-time employed residents in similar occupation groups at around 10% instead.

sections.label: Marital immunity for rape repealed
sections.summary: The Bill will repeal marital immunity for rape.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Bill will repeal marital immunity for rape.

sections.label: SCWO seed fund
sections.summary: SCWO is an umbrella women's organisation with over 500,000 women in its 50-member organisations, and OWD will introduce a seed fund for it to administer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: SCWO is the umbrella women’s organisation with over 500,000 women in its 50-member organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that OWD will introduce a seed fund for SCWO to administer.

sections.label: Tripartite Taskforce on social work
sections.summary: The Tripartite Taskforce brings together representatives from the social work ecosystem, and it needs time to meet before recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his interest in the Tripartite Taskforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This Tripartite Taskforce brings together representatives from the entire ecosystem, naqmely, those who train our social workers, both pre-employment as well as mid-career; those who employ and work with social workers in our VWOs and agencies; and of course, the Government departments as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, if he senses that we need more social work intervention, say, in the geriatric field, and we will go on to work with our academic partners to see how the curriculum can be adjusted in order to cater to this growing need, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, as to when we can start to expect some recommendations to come out from the tripartite task force, let us give them a bit of time to meet.

sections.label: Social work career transition
sections.summary: Many enter social work from pre-employment training in polytechnics and universities, and career transition is being strengthened for older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Many come from pre-employment training from polytechnics and our universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But I am also seeing how we can further strengthen career transition for older workers with life experience who want to go into social work.

sections.label: Childcare centres joining CMS
sections.summary: All ECDA-regulated childcare centres and kindergartens will come on board CMS, with rollout to all preschools likely later this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: All childcare centres and kindergartens regulated by ECDA under the Early Childhood Development Centres Act will come on board CMS and we are likely going to roll out to all preschools later this year.

sections.label: Appeals and universal schemes
sections.summary: Appeals and re-appeals are a long journey, but schemes benefiting all Singaporean children apply regardless of parents' marital status.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Usually, we will appeal and re-appeal, but then it is really a very long circuitous journey for these people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On the former, as I said earlier, schemes that benefit all children, all Singaporean children, apply across the board, regardless of the marital status of the parents.

sections.label: Preschools with one-year extension
sections.summary: A question asks the Senior Parliamentary Secretary how many preschools received a one-year extension and still await the licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One is: could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share with us the number of preschools that have been given the one-year extension and are still awaiting the licence he had referred to?

sections.label: Lien Foundation early childhood report
sections.summary: The Lien Foundation report benchmarked Singapore's early childhood against other countries; accessibility ranked poorly as preschool is not legally mandated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Just to supplement my colleague's response, the Lien Foundation report benchmarked early childhood in Singapore with that in a number of other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On accessibility, I understand we did not rank well because we did not legally mandate that every child go to preschool even though our preschool attendance rate is very high, even for those with lower socio-economic status (SES).

sections.label: Social Service Offices weekend operations
sections.summary: The speaker asked whether Social Service Offices should operate on weekends, noting three SSOs are open on Saturdays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In a quest to provide more comprehensive, more coordinated, more convenient services to residents, I have asked in my cut yesterday and previously whether our Social Service Offices (SSOs) should also consider operating during the weekends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have three SSOs that are open on Saturdays.

sections.label: ComLink centres and rental families
sections.summary: For four ComLink centres opening over the next two years, the aim is to reach 14,000 families in rental housing with young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of ComLink which I articulated yesterday, for the four centres that we will open in the course of the next two years, we hope to reach out to 14,000 families in rental housing with young children, and work with them proactively.

sections.label: SSOs open on Saturdays
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies that four SSOs, not three, are open on Saturdays on a half-day basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Maybe before I respond to Ms Tin Pei Ling, I also want to make a clarification in response to Mr Seah Kian Peng.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is not three but four SSOs that are open on Saturdays, half-day.

sections.label: Accurate triangulation of means
sections.summary: One aim is to triangulate more accurately to determine means for specific applications such as ComCare and other support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One is to make sure that, in relation to specific applications, say, for ComCare and other forms of support by clients and beneficiaries, we should be able to have a more accurate triangulation to determine means.

sections.label: Difference between CKS and PDD
sections.summary: PDD helps persons who lost mental capacity for major decisions, while CKS involves VWO partners helping seniors with daily living activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The difference between CKS and PDD is that PDD helps persons who have lost the mental capacity to make major decisions like liquidating the assets, bank accounts and all that to provide institutional care or some other major financial needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Whereas CKS is to involve VWO partners in the community to help seniors who have lost their mental capacities to deal with the day-to-day living activities, like buying food, getting monies to pay for services likes utilities and so on.
